body: Fossils preserve parts of past bodies. Comparisons of bone shape and geological dating help place them in time. Fossils from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco show a combination of older and more recent-looking traits. Researchers reported a date of roughly 315,000 years, with a stated uncertainty of 34,000 years, for heated stone artifacts from associated deposits.

Early Homo sapiens lived in Africa. Evidence from fossils, archaeology and ancestry shows people later spread to other continents. Repeated movement, separation and contact shaped human populations. Today's shared ancestry and diversity reflect many of these histories.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: A site dates particular evidence. It does not mark the instant a species began. Population history and the times and paths of some migrations remain under investigation.
purpose: Use fossils, archaeology and genetics to explain migration with uncertainty.
